mainTopic: Agents who change their instructions (גט and עירוב), which words from a husband order a גט, and a man in danger who says only 'write'
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier case: the גט works only once the agent reaches מתא מחסיא. The גמרא then asks why רבי אלעזר needs to forbid a woman to eat תרומה right away when she only told her agent where to receive her גט. It answers that he teaches this even where the agent walked the wrong way, because he might have met the husband by chance. Next come two ברייתות that disagree about an agent who made an עירוב with a different fruit than he was told. רבה says they follow רבנן and רבי אלעזר. רב יוסף says both follow רבנן, and the ruling depends on whose fruit it was. He defends this against אביי's tower and dovecote case. A new משנה then lists which words from a husband clearly order a גט and which mean nothing, with רבי נתן and רבא explaining פַּטְּרוּהָ versus פִּיטְרוּהָ. Finally, a משנה teaches that a man in danger who says only 'write a גט' means 'write and give.' The גמרא begins the story of גניבא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The divorce only works once the agent reaches מתא מחסיא
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the previous case: the גט does not take effect until the agent arrives in מתא מחסיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a valid גט until you reach מתא מחסיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the case it was discussing just before this. The ruling is that the גט does not take effect until the agent gets to the town of מתא מחסיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The location named here works like a real condition. The divorce only starts once the agent arrives at that place. This is the background for the next step, where the question is whether naming a place is a real condition or just directions.

keyTerms.meaning: A גט, a bill of divorce
A town in Babylonia, near סורא

phrases.english: It is not a valid bill of divorce
until you reach Mata Meḥasya.

steps.triggerLanguage: גִּיטָּא לָא הָוֵי עַד דְּמָטֵית לְמָתָא מַחְסֵיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous discussion, which started before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: When the place really is a condition, the גט does not take effect until the agent arrives there.

steps.title: Why does רבי אלעזר need to say this? It seems obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אלעזר's ruling in the משנה and asks why it is needed, since the woman was only telling the agent where to go.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבי אלעזר forbids her to eat תרומה right away. The גמרא asks: That is obvious! She is only showing him where to find the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, where a woman told her agent, 'Receive my גט in such and such a place.' רבי אלעזר says she must stop eating תרומה right away, and the גמרא asks why he even needs to say that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman did not make the divorce depend on that place. She only gave directions to where her husband is. So the agent could get the גט anywhere, and of course she must worry it already happened. The question is: what new thing is רבי אלעזר teaching?

keyTerms.meaning: Forbids right away. Here it means she may no longer eat תרומה from now on.
It is obvious, so why say it?
Only pointing out a place, not making a condition

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the woman's words as a condition. In this case the place is only directions, and that is exactly why the גמרא thinks רבי אלעזר's ruling is obvious.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar prohibits immediately.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה. She's married to a כהן, and once she may be divorced she can't eat תרומה anymore.

phrases.aramaic: פְּשִׁיטָא, דְּהָא מַרְאָה מָקוֹם הִיא לוֹ!
phrases.english: That is obvious, as she is merely indicating a place to him!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא, דְּהָא מַרְאָה מָקוֹם הִיא לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by going back to a line from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that she is forbidden right away
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Naming a place was only directions, not a condition, so of course the גט could be received anywhere at any time. The ruling seems to add nothing new.

steps.title: Even if the agent walked the wrong way, he might have met the husband
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed for a case where the agent went west even though the husband is in the east. Even so, he may have run into the husband and been given the גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where she told him, 'Go east, because he is in the east,' and the agent went west. You might think: the husband is not in the west, so nothing could have happened. רבי אלעזר teaches us that maybe while the agent was walking, he ran into the husband, and the husband gave him the גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר is teaching an unusual case. The agent went in the opposite direction from the husband, and still she must stop eating תרומה right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought that an agent walking away from the husband certainly will not get the גט soon. רבי אלעזר says we still worry that the agent met the husband by chance along the way. This is the new point that makes his ruling needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for a case where...
He ran into him by chance

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אלעזר, naming a place is only directions. Even if the agent heads the wrong way, she must worry that he met the husband and got the גט, so she stops eating תרומה right away.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary where she said to him:
"Go to the east, as he is in the east";
and he went to the west.
Lest you say: in the west, he is not there;
he teaches us,
that perhaps while he was going,
he encountered him,
and he gave him the bill of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'it is obvious' question by narrowing רבי אלעזר's ruling to a specific case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the agent went away from the husband, he surely will not receive the גט soon, so she could keep eating תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even then we worry that he met the husband by chance and received the גט, so she is forbidden right away.

steps.title: Two ברייתות disagree about an agent who made an עירוב with the wrong fruit
steps.stepSummary: A man asked his agent to make an עירוב with dates, and the agent used dried figs, or the other way around. One ברייתא says the עירוב works, and another says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone tells his agent, 'Make an עירוב for me with dates,' and he makes it with dried figs, or 'with dried figs,' and he makes it with dates: one ברייתא teaches that his עירוב is valid, and another ברייתא teaches that his עירוב is not valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related case of an agent who did not follow his instructions exactly, this time about an עירוב. It shows two ברייתות that contradict each other, which sets up a resolution that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the agent changed the kind of fruit, not the direction he walked. One ברייתא ignores the change and says the עירוב works. The other says that changing the instructions ruins the mission. The גמרא now needs to explain how both can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: Here an עירוב תחומין: food placed to let a person walk further on שבת
One ברייתא teaches... and another ברייתא teaches...

steps.whyThisMatters: This contradiction shows the bigger question behind the whole section: when does an agent who changes his instructions still count as the sender's agent?

phrases.english: One who says to his agent: "Establish an eiruv for me with dates,"
and he established an eiruv for him with dried figs;
"with dried figs," and he established an eiruv for him with dates;
it is taught in one baraita: his eiruv is a valid eiruv,
and it is taught in another: his eiruv is not a valid eiruv!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: עֵירוּבוֹ עֵירוּב, וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: אֵין עֵירוּבוֹ עֵירוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a related topic about an agent who changed his instructions, this time with an עירוב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about the agent who used a different fruit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both ברייתות describe the same case but give opposite rulings, so they seem to contradict each other.

steps.title: רבה: the two ברייתות follow two different opinions
steps.stepSummary: רבה says one ברייתא follows רבנן, who hold the sender insists on his exact words. The other follows רבי אלעזר, who holds the sender was only making a suggestion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: There is no contradiction. One ברייתא follows רבנן and the other follows רבי אלעזר. רבנן say the sender insists on his exact instructions. רבי אלעזר says she was only showing him a place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the contradiction between the two עירוב ברייתות. He says they follow the same two opinions we saw in the גט case of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן hold that when a person gives an agent instructions, he insists on them. If the agent changes anything, he is no longer acting for the sender, so the עירוב does not work. רבי אלעזר holds that the instruction was only a suggestion, like the woman who was just telling the agent where to go. So for him, the change does not matter and the עירוב works.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
Insistence: the sender cares that his exact instruction be followed
Just showing a place; a suggestion, not a condition

phrases.english: Rabba said: It is not difficult;
this one is the Rabbis, that one is Rabbi Elazar.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא that says the עירוב doesn't work follows רבנן; the one that says it works follows רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: This one is the Rabbis, who say: there is insistence;
that one is Rabbi Elazar, who says:
she is just showing him a place.
phrases.notes: "She" is the woman from our משנה who told the agent where to receive her גט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between the ברייתות raised in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each ברייתא follows a different תנא (a dispute between תנאים).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two ברייתות about the same case seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not valid = רבנן (the sender insists). Valid = רבי אלעזר (only a suggestion).

steps.title: רב יוסף: both follow רבנן, but whose fruit was it?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says both ברייתות follow רבנן. If the fruit was the sender's own, the עירוב works. If it was someone else's, it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Both ברייתות follow רבנן. One is talking about the sender's own fruit, and the other is talking about his friend's fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a different answer. He does not split the ברייתות between two opinions. Instead, he says they are talking about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the fruit is the sender's own, he does not really mind which kind is used, so the עירוב works. When the fruit belongs to someone else, that owner only allowed one kind of fruit, so using the other kind is not allowed and the עירוב fails. This way, רבנן can hold both rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: With his friend's (fruit), belonging to someone else
This one and that one; both

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:
both this one and that one are the Rabbis;
here, it is with his own fruit,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that says the עירוב works.

phrases.english: there, it is with his friend's fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: הָא וְהָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same contradiction, different from רבה's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting into two different cases (own fruit vs. another person's fruit).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות must reflect two different opinions.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow רבנן. The ruling depends on who owns the fruit.

steps.title: אביי asks about the tower and the dovecote
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings two more ברייתות that disagree about an agent told to make an עירוב in a tower who made it in a dovecote. Here, he asks, how can the difference be about whose fruit it is?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: What about the ברייתא of a person who told his agent, "Make an עירוב for me in the tower," and he made it in the dovecote, or "in the dovecote," and he made it in the tower? One ברייתא teaches that the עירוב works, and another teaches that it does not. There, what difference between his own and his friend's could there be?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's answer. He points to a similar contradiction where the change seems to be about a place, not about fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the change seems to be only about where the עירוב is placed. So רב יוסף's split between "his own fruit" and "his friend's fruit" does not seem to fit. אביי's point is that רב יוסף's answer seems unable to explain this second pair of ברייתות.

keyTerms.meaning: Dovecote, a place where doves are kept
His עירוב is a valid עירוב

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But what about that which was taught in a baraita:
One who says to his agent:
"Make an eiruv for me in the tower,"
and he made it for him in the dovecote;
or "in the dovecote," and he made it for him in the tower;
one baraita teaches: his eiruv is a valid eiruv,
and another baraita teaches: his eiruv is not a valid eiruv;

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם – מַאי שֶׁלּוֹ וְשֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ אִיכָּא?
phrases.english: there, what "his own" or "his friend's" is there?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's answer from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's split between the sender's own fruit and another person's fruit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A parallel contradiction about the location of an עירוב cannot be explained by fruit ownership, so רב יוסף's answer seems to fail.

steps.title: There too, it is about whose fruit to use
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that "tower" and "dovecote" mean the fruit stored in the tower and the fruit stored in the dovecote. So רב יוסף's split works there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, there is fruit of the tower and fruit of the dovecote.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יוסף. It explains that the tower and dovecote ברייתות are also about fruit, not about a place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sender was not telling the agent where to put the עירוב. He was telling him which fruit to take: the fruit kept in the tower or the fruit kept in the dovecote. So the same split applies. If both stores of fruit were the sender's own, the עירוב works. If they belonged to someone else, it does not.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה: the ברייתות follow רבנן (the sender insists) vs. רבי אלעזר (only a suggestion). רב יוסף: both follow רבנן, and the ruling depends on whether the fruit was the sender's own or someone else's. This even works for the tower/dovecote case, because there too the instruction was about which fruit to take.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read "in the tower" as the place where the עירוב is put. According to this answer, it means which fruit to use: the fruit stored in the tower.

phrases.english: There too,
there is fruit of the tower
phrases.notes: The instruction was about which fruit to take, not about where to put the עירוב.

phrases.english: and fruit of the dovecote.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם נָמֵי, אִיכָּא פֵּירֵי דְמִגְדָּל וּפֵירֵי דְשׁוֹבָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge and keeps רב יוסף's approach standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: tower/dovecote means the fruit stored there.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The instruction was about where to place the עירוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The instruction was about which fruit to use, so the split between own fruit and someone else's fruit applies.

steps.title: Phrases that clearly mean divorce
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if a husband says 'Write a גט and give it to my wife,' 'Divorce her,' or 'Write a letter and give it to her,' the people he spoke to should write the גט and give it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man says: 'Write a גט and give it to my wife,' or 'Divorce her,' or 'Write a letter and give it to her,' they should write it and give it to her.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It lists three things a husband can say that clearly tell people to divorce his wife for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase shows plainly that the husband wants a divorce. Because his meaning is clear, the people he spoke to may write the גט and give it to her. Even 'a letter' counts, because in this setting it obviously means a גט.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who says: "Write a bill of divorce
and give it to my wife";
or "Divorce her";
or "Write a letter and give it to her" –
these people should write it and give it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins on a new topic. The earlier steps about עירוב are finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Clear words of divorce allow the people he spoke to to write and give the גט.

steps.title: Phrases that are too unclear to count
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: 'Release her,' 'Support her,' 'Treat her according to the law,' or 'Treat her properly' mean nothing, so no גט is given.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said: 'Release her,' 'Support her,' 'Treat her according to the law,' or 'Treat her properly,' he has said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now lists phrases that do not work, because they do not clearly mean divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these phrases could mean something other than divorce. 'Support her' could mean giving her food. 'Release her' could mean freeing her from some duty. Since the husband's wish to divorce is not clear, the people he spoke to may not act.

keyTerms.meaning: Support her (give her food and needs)
According to the law or custom
He said nothing; his words have no effect

steps.whatToRemember: A husband's instruction works only if his words clearly mean divorce. Words with more than one meaning do nothing.

phrases.english: But if he said "Release her"; or "Support her";
or "Treat her according to the law";
phrases.notes: נִימוּס is a Greek word meaning law or custom.

phrases.english: or "Treat her properly" –
he has said nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״פַּטְּרוּהָ״; ״פַּרְנְסוּהָ״; ״עֲשׂוּ לָהּ כְּנִימוּס״; ״עֲשׂוּ לָהּ כָּרָאוּי״ – לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the other half of the משנה's list: the phrases that do not work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Phrases that do not clearly mean divorce have no effect.

steps.title: A ברייתא adds more divorce phrases
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says 'Send her away,' 'Leave her,' and 'Drive her out' all work. It repeats that 'Release her,' 'Support her,' and the other two phrases mean nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'Send her away,' 'Leave her,' 'Drive her out' – they should write and give the גט. 'Release her,' 'Support her,' 'Treat her according to the law,' 'Treat her properly' – he said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds three more phrases that clearly mean divorce. It repeats the משנה's list of phrases that do not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new phrases all mean sending the wife away, which is what divorce is. The ברייתא lists פַּטְּרוּהָ among the phrases that do not work, just like the משנה. This sets up רבי נתן's different view in the next step.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
"Send her away"; "Leave her"; "Drive her out" –
these people should write it and give it.
"Release her"; "Support her";
"Treat her according to the law"; "Treat her properly" –
he has said nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא adds more examples to the משנה's two lists.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Phrases meaning 'send her away' work like 'divorce her.' פַּטְּרוּהָ and the other unclear phrases do not work.

steps.title: רבי נתן: one pronunciation works, the other does not
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן says that if the husband said פַּטְּרוּהָ, his words count. If he said פִּיטְרוּהָ, he said nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: 'פַּטְּרוּהָ' (release her) – his words stand. 'פִּיטְרוּהָ' (exempt her) – he said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: Another ברייתא brings רבי נתן. He splits the word into two pronunciations: one counts as divorce and one does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה and the first ברייתא said פַּטְּרוּהָ does nothing. רבי נתן says פַּטְּרוּהָ does work, because it means 'release her,' which fits divorce. Only פִּיטְרוּהָ ('exempt her') does nothing. So רבי נתן seems to disagree with our תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: His words stand; they take effect

steps.confusionAlert: The two words are spelled almost the same way. The only difference is the vowels: פַּטְּרוּהָ (patruha) and פִּיטְרוּהָ (pitruha).

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Natan says:
If he said "Patruha" – his words stand,
phrases.notes: פַּטְּרוּהָ means 'release her,' which fits a divorce.

phrases.english: if he said "Pitruha" – he has said nothing.
phrases.notes: פִּיטְרוּהָ means 'exempt her,' which has nothing to do with divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: ״פַּטְּרוּהָ״ – דְּבָרָיו קַיָּימִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי נתן seems to disagree with the משנה and the ברייתא about the word פַּטְּרוּהָ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פַּטְּרוּהָ counts as divorce, but פִּיטְרוּהָ does not.

steps.title: רבא: the difference comes from how people spoke
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי נתן was from בבל, where people told פִּיטְרוּהָ and פַּטְּרוּהָ apart. Our תנא was from ארץ ישראל, where people did not tell them apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי נתן is from בבל, so he tells apart פִּיטְרוּהָ and פַּטְּרוּהָ. Our תנא is from ארץ ישראל, so he does not tell them apart.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why רבי נתן and our משנה seem to disagree about פַּטְּרוּהָ. The difference is how people spoke in each place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בבל, people said the two words differently, so each word had its own meaning. There, פַּטְּרוּהָ clearly meant 'release her.' In ארץ ישראל, people did not separate the two sounds, so the word could also mean 'exempt her' and was not clear enough. This explains the gap between them as a matter of local speech.

keyTerms.meaning: He is careful to tell apart
Our תנא (the author of our משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: Whether a phrase counts as divorce depends on what it clearly means to the people who speak that way. Even a small difference in pronunciation can change the meaning.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the words of a גט instruction are judged by how people actually talk in that place.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Rabbi Natan is a Babylonian,
and he distinguishes between "pitruha" and "patruha";

phrases.aramaic: תַּנָּא דִּידַן – דְּבַר אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא,
phrases.english: our tanna is from Eretz Yisrael,
so he does not distinguish between them.
phrases.notes: In his way of speaking, the two words sounded alike, so פַּטְּרוּהָ was not clearly about divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: רַבִּי נָתָן – דְּבַבְלָאָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This explains the apparent gap between רבי נתן in step 12 and the משנה in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The difference is explained by regional speech habits.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי נתן and our תנא seem to disagree about whether פַּטְּרוּהָ counts as divorce.
steps.terutzMaskana: In בבל the two words sounded different, so פַּטְּרוּהָ clearly meant 'release her.' In ארץ ישראל they sounded alike, so the word was unclear and did nothing.

steps.title: Six more phrases: do they count?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask about six more phrases a husband might use and whether each one counts as an order to give a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: If the husband said 'Remove her,' what is the law? 'Abandon her'? 'Unbind her'? 'Let her be'? 'Be useful for her'? 'Treat her according to the custom'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists six phrases that are not clear, and asks whether each one is strong enough to count as an order to write and give a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 9–11 showed that some phrases clearly mean divorce and others mean nothing. These six phrases are in the middle: each could mean divorce, or each could mean something else, like caring for her. The question is which side each one falls on.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (the חכמים)

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
If he said 'Remove her,' what is the law?
'Abandon her,' what is the law?
'Unbind her,' what is the law?
'Let her be,' what is the law?
'Be useful for her,' what is the law?
phrases.notes: He could mean 'help her get free of me,' or just 'help her out' with her needs.

phrases.english: 'Treat her according to the custom,' what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא explained רבי נתן's view on פטרוה, the גמרא moves on to more unclear phrases.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does each of these six phrases count as an order to write and give a גט?

steps.title: One phrase is resolved: 'Treat her according to the custom' means nothing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא settles just one of the six: 'Treat her according to the custom' does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Resolve at least one of them, as a ברייתא teaches: 'Treat her according to the custom,' 'Treat her according to the law,' 'Treat her properly' — he said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers only the last of the six questions by quoting a ברייתא that says 'Treat her according to the custom' means nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts כדת together with כנימוס and כראוי, which the משנה already said mean nothing. So כדת also means nothing, and no גט is given. The other five phrases are left without an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Resolve at least one (of the questions)
According to the custom / the accepted way
He said nothing (his words have no effect)

steps.confusionAlert: Only ONE of the six questions is answered here. Do not assume the other five phrases also mean nothing; the גמרא leaves them open.

phrases.english: Resolve at least one, as it is taught in a ברייתא:
'Treat her according to the custom';
'Treat her according to the law';
'Treat her properly' — he said nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the last of the six questions from step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא puts 'עשו לה כדת' next to phrases that mean nothing, so it also means nothing. The other five stay unresolved.

steps.title: New משנה: a man led out to execution who only says 'write'
steps.stepSummary: If a man led out to execution says only 'Write a גט for my wife,' they write it and also give it. Later this was extended to someone setting sail or leaving with a caravan.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first they said: One who is led out in a neck chain and says 'Write a גט for my wife' — they should write it and give it. Then they said: Also one who sets sail, and one who leaves with a caravan.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה teaches that in some urgent situations, the words 'write a גט' alone are enough, and they also give it to the wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a husband has to say both 'write' and 'give' (step 9). A man about to be executed is under pressure and clearly wants the divorce finished, so 'write' is understood to include 'give.' The later ruling applies the same idea to people going on dangerous journeys.

keyTerms.meaning: One led out in a neck chain (to be executed)
They then said (a later, wider ruling)
One who leaves with a caravan

steps.confusionAlert: The new point is that he said only 'write' and did not say 'give.' Even so, they give the גט.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea that a man's situation can show what he really wants, even when his words leave something out.

phrases.english: משנה: At first they would say:
One who is led out in a neck chain,
phrases.notes: This is a man being taken to be executed by the government.

phrases.english: and said: 'Write a גט for my wife' —
these people should write it and give it.
They then said:
Also one who sets sail, and one who leaves with a caravan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It builds on step 9, where the husband said both 'write' and 'give.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man led out to execution, and later also someone setting sail or leaving with a caravan, who says only 'write a גט' is understood to mean 'write and give.'

steps.title: רבי שמעון שזורי adds one who is dangerously ill
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון שזורי says the same rule applies to someone who is dangerously ill.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון שזורי says: Also one who is dangerously ill.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון שזורי widens the list once more, to a man who is very sick and in danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A seriously ill man is also facing possible death, just like the cases already listed. So if he says only 'write a גט,' we understand that he also means 'give it.'
steps.whatToRemember: In danger cases (קולר, setting sail, caravan, and for רבי שמעון שזורי also a dangerously ill man), 'write a גט' alone is enough, and they give it too.

phrases.english: רבי שמעון שזורי says:
Also one who is dangerously ill.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי אוֹמֵר: אַף הַמְסוּכָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more case to the list in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון שזורי, a dangerously ill man who says 'write a גט' is also understood to mean 'write and give.'

steps.title: The story of גניבא led out to execution
steps.stepSummary: גניבא, on his way to execution, ordered 400 זוזים to be given to רבי אבינא from his wine in נהר פניא. רבי זירא is about to comment.
steps.simpleTranslation: גניבא was led out in a neck chain. As he was going out, he said: Give four hundred זוזים to רבי אבינא from the wine in נהר פניא. רבי זירא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a man in the משנה's exact situation, led out to execution, who gave an instruction about his money. It is setting up a comment by רבי זירא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that a man led out in a קולר is understood to mean more than he said. Here such a man gives an instruction about money instead of a גט. The text breaks off at 'רבי זירא said', so his comment comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who was led out to execution
A place where גניבא had wine

phrases.english: גמרא: גניבא was being led out in a neck chain,
When he was going out, he said:

phrases.aramaic: הַבוּ אַרְבַּע מְאָה זוּזֵי לְרַבִּי אֲבִינָא,
phrases.english: Give four hundred זוזים to רבי אבינא,
from the wine in נהר פניא.
phrases.notes: He means: pay it out of the wine he owns in that place.

phrases.english: רבי זירא said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא's first discussion of the משנה's case of a man led out in a קולר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup story: גניבא, while being led to execution, ordered 400 זוזים to be given to רבי אבינא from his wine. רבי זירא's comment follows.
